'''''Kalanchoe delagoensis''''', formerly known as '''''Bryophyllum delagoense'''''<ref name="Rafter-et-al-2008" /> and commonly called '''mother of millions''' or '''chandelier plant''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> is a [[succulent plant]] native to [[Madagascar]]. Like other members of ''[[Bryophyllum]]'' (now included in ''[[Kalanchoe]]''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=''Kalanchoe delagoensis'' Eckl. & Zeyh.|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:274320-1|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-14|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=Kew Science}}</ref>), it is able to propagate [[Vegetative reproduction|vegetatively]] from plantlets that develop on its leaf margins.

==Description==
[[File:Kalanchoe tubiflora01.jpg|thumb|left|Flowers]]
[[File:Kalanchoe delagoensis (Habitus).jpg|thumb|right|Habitus]]
It is a robust, completely bare, [[biennial plant|biennial]] or more or less [[perennial]], succulent plant that reaches heights of between 0.2 and 2 meters. The upright stems are simple and round. The three-seated, seemingly opposite or alternate leaves are usually upright to straight when spread out. They are slightly cylindrical, a little rutty on the top and reach a length of 1 to 13 centimeters with a diameter of 2 to 6 millimeters. The leaf blade narrowed at the base is reddish-green to gray-green with reddish brown spots. At the tip of the leaf margin there are two to nine small teeth on which there are numerous brood buds.

===Inflorescences===
The compact, multi-flowered inflorescences form [[thyrse]]s 10 to 25 centimeters long. The slender [[Pedicel (botany)|flower stalk]] is between 6 and 20 millimeters long. The [[hermaphrodite]] flowers are hanging. The reddish to green and red-striped petals are fused together like a bell. The 2.5 to 6 millimeter long [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] tube ends in sharply pointed, triangular-lanceolate corolla lobes 5 to 10 millimeters long and 3.7 to 5.7 millimeters wide. The [[stamen]]s are attached below the center of the corolla tube and do not protrude beyond the tube. The 2 to 2.5 millimeters large [[anthers]] are egg-shaped. The [[nectar]] flakes, 0.7 to 2 centimeters long are half-round to square with a rounded tip. The oval-elongated carpel is 5.5 to 6.5 millimeters long. The [[stylus]] has a length of about 2 millimeters.
[[File:Kalanchoe delagoensis in Dapeng Fortress, Shenzhen.jpg|thumb|''Kalanchoe delagoensis'' in Dapeng Fortress, Shenzhen]]
The upright [[follicle (fruit)|follicles]] contain seeds with a diameter of 0.6 to 2.5 millimeters.

==Invasive species==
This species' capability for [[vegetative reproduction]], its [[drought tolerance]], and its popularity as a [[ornamental plant|garden plant]], relate to this species' becoming an [[invasive weed]] in places such as [[eastern Australia]], [[South Africa]]<ref>{{cite web |title=''Invasive Species South Africa, Chandelier plant'' | url=https://invasives.org.za/fact-sheet/?wpv_post_search&wpv-wpcf-scientific-name=Bryophyllum+delagoense+%28Crassulaceae%29}}</ref> and many [[Pacific islands]]. In the [[Neotropics]] [[hummingbird]]s sometimes pollinate this non-native plant.<ref>For example [[sapphire-spangled emerald]] (''Amazilia lactea'') in Brazil (Baza Mendonça & dos Anjos 2005)</ref>

''Kalanchoe delagoensis'' is unwelcome because it displaces native plants and contains [[bufadienolide]] [[cardiac glycosides]]<ref>[[Bryotoxin]]s A, B and C: McKenzie ''et al.'' (1987), Steyn & van Heerden (1998)</ref> which can cause fatal poisoning, particularly in grazing animals like cattle.<ref>McKenzie & Dunster (1986), McKenzie ''et al.'' (1987)</ref> During 1997, 125 head of cattle died after eating this species on a [[Stock route|travelling stock reserve]] near [[Moree, New South Wales|Moree, NSW]].<ref>{{cite web |author=les tanner |url=http://www.northwestweeds.nsw.gov.au/mother_of_millions.htm |title=North West Weeds |publisher=Northwestweeds.nsw.gov.au |accessdate=2013-02-19 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090621015741/http://northwestweeds.nsw.gov.au/mother_of_millions.htm |archivedate=2009-06-21 }}</ref>

In the Australian states of New South Wales<ref>{{cite web |title=''The New South Wales Government WeedWise Resource'' | url=https://weeds.dpi.nsw.gov.au/Weeds/MotherOfMillions}}</ref> and Queensland,<ref>{{cite web |title=''The Queensland Government Resource on invasive plants'' | url=https://www.business.qld.gov.au/industries/farms-fishing-forestry/agriculture/land-management/health-pests-weeds-diseases/weeds-diseases/invasive-plants/restricted/mother-millions}}</ref> this species and its hybrids have been declared a noxious weed.
